clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2 at reth v2.11.0: the key of each execution cache entry and where every cached value comes from.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs on 2026-11-27. Lines 963-971 key code by B256, storage by (Address, StorageKey) and accounts by Address. insert_state (lines 1133-1206) writes slot.present_value of every slot of each modified account from the block BundleState and the final account info. should_fill_on_miss (lines 276-278) gates every get_or_try_insert path in basic_account, storage and bytecode_by_hash (lines 846-941), and the LookupOnly branch returns the provider value without inserting it. A txpool snapshot hit returns before the cache is touched, so a snapshot value is never inserted. clear() (lines 1213-1219) empties storage and accounts only. I did not read payload_validator.rs lines 650-690 for the list of FillOnMiss paths; the prewarm constructors at prewarm.rs lines 800-806 and 920-928 use new_prewarm over the parent provider as the item says.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2 at reth v2.11.0: when the cross-block cache is kept, replaced or dropped after a block.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_processor/prewarm.rs. run() (lines 653-715) calls save_cache only after both Terminate and FinishedTxExecution have arrived. FinishedTxExecution is sent by spawn_txs_prewarm only after in_place_scope returns and refresh_results ends (lines 157-253), and by run_bal_prewarm only after pool.end_block() and the streaming task signal (lines 538-640). A prewarm worker therefore cannot insert a parent-state value after save_cache has applied the block's post-state. save_cache (lines 468-517) applies insert_state under the mutex and takes the stored cache out on an insert error or a closed valid_block_rx. I did not reread lib.rs get_cache_for or mod.rs on_inserted_executed_block. The live comparison below independently shows no stale PoolManager word on Ethereum, Base and Unichain.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3: on one endpoint per reth-derived network, eth_getStorageAt against extsload(bytes32[]) through eth_call for PoolManager slots written in the newest blocks, at the writing block B and at B+1, and against the last Swap event of each pool in B.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran a smaller version with my own script on 2026-11-27 against https://mainnet.unichain.org (op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4-65e80332), https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc) and https://base-rpc.publicnode.com (reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd base/v1.5.6). For the last Swap of 15 pool and block pairs per network in the 400 blocks before head, the slot0 word (keccak(poolId, 6), POOLS_SLOT at src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:11, mapping at src/PoolManager.sol:93) and the liquidity word (offset 3) read the same through eth_getStorageAt and through extsload at B and B+1, and at B the sqrtPriceX96, tick and liquidity equal the Swap event. 90 of 90 reads matched. The deployed PoolManagers are the public v4 deployments, so this tests the node, not the CTF bytecode. src/ outside src/test has no SELFDESTRUCT or DELEGATECALL, so the destroyed-account cache branch cannot reach the PoolManager.
